problems.problem: The regenerated plane still breaks into stacked bands instead of the briefed single wet sheet: a hard horizontal seam crosses the full width at ~y655-665 (above mid-frame, contradicting '天际线压低在画面下三分之一'), and a speckled darker dry-sand strip with a soft crease returns across the bottom ~y1290-1440. The bottle therefore stands on a mid-frame grey shelf while a different material occupies the foreground, unlike references 3-5 where one coherent ground/space carries the subject.

Contact detail crop [484,1012,941,1262] confirms the contact shadow exists at offset_y 0 directly under the base - correctly aligned, not floating, do not shift down. But it renders as a thin hard dark slit (~x620-800, i.e. ~60% of the visible glass footprint x564-861) with a crisp edge, so the base reads pinched onto a line instead of settled into wet sand; width_scale 1.25 evidently did not broaden the alpha footprint. The brief's '倒影没入水面' mirror reflection is still absent: flat grey water surrounds the base with no vertical reflection gradient, so the water never acts as the narrative light source.

Luminance mismatch persists: the unmodified packshot carries soft diffuse frontal studio light with bright cap dome and shoulder highlights, yet the backdrop's brightest zone is the upper sky and the water plane darkens steadily toward the base (~mid-grey at y1150). The bottle's luminance floats above its immediate surround with no supporting bounce from the plane, whereas references 4-5 deliberately match subject and ground luminance.

The sand-gold divider rule (decoration x454,y430,width2) still renders as a ~2x8px orange speck right of the 'Dior' logo / above the title - visible in the poster as a stray dot, not as the intended vertical water-mark rule separating the inscription column from the image column. As drawn it reads as a render artifact and weakens the two-column editorial grid.

Column rhythm improved (subtitle now anchors the foot at y1040), but the stele block still reads split: title bottom 608 to subtitle top 1040 is a 432px void with no intermediate measure, while logo-to-title is only 88px; the left column therefore lacks the continuous coastal-inscription cadence the brief describes, and the subtitle sits close to the water seam at y~660? no - it sits isolated in flat grey with only the seam far above, giving the column foot no visual anchor.
